evidence.intent_output: A RED test would have shown a regression from the fix. All 8 probe cases are GREEN: HTTP/1.0 100 then HTTP/1.1 200 chunked is decoded as 'hello'; HTTP/1.1 100 then HTTP/1.0 200 chunked is 502 INVALID_RESPONSE; HTTP/1.0 with bare-LF line ends and TE is 502; HTTP/1.0 HEAD with TE + Content-Length: 10 relays Content-Length 10, no body, no error; HTTP/1.0 304 with TE + CL is bodyless with no error; HTTP/1.0 with Content-Length: 5 relays 'hello' with Content-Length 5; HTTP/1.9 chunked is still decoded; HTTP/1.0 TE gzip is 502.

findings.drop_reason: Regression hunt for the FND-001 fix (interim-head version mixing, bare-LF status lines, HEAD/304 over HTTP/1.0 with TE+CL per FR-PROXY-014 AC-6, HTTP/1.0 Content-Length and read-until-close, HTTP/1.x minor > 1) found no defect: every probe case behaves as required, so there is nothing to keep.
findings.title: No regression from the HTTP/1.0 Transfer-Encoding rejection
findings.description: The http10 flag is taken from the final head's own status line (interim heads do not leak), the check sits after the HEAD/204/304 bodyless branch so FR-PROXY-014 AC-6 is kept, and HTTP/1.0 responses without TE are unaffected.

evidence.output: Pre-fix framing() already threw 'Content-Length with Transfer-Encoding' for TE+CL on a body-capable response; HEAD/204/304 and no-framing-header HTTP/1.0 cases were already handled before the fix.

findings.drop_reason: Of the six new tests only sec_PROXY_004_transferEncodingOnHttp10ResponseIsInvalidResponse was RED before the fix; the TE+CL, HEAD, 204, 304 and no-framing tests already passed on the old code. They are guard tests that pin the bodyless order and HTTP/1.0 read-until-close around the new branch, which is legitimate, and the fix itself is covered by the RED test. The TE+CL test does not tell 'HTTP/1.0 check' apart from 'CL with TE check', but the outcome (502 INVALID_RESPONSE) is the required one either way. Not a defect.
findings.title: Five of six new tests were already green before the fix
findings.description: Guard tests rather than fix-discriminating tests; acceptable.
